content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Fresno

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: Verify you meet PMI's education and project-management experience requirements for the PMP credential. You'll need either a bachelor's degree plus documented hours managing projects, or a high school diploma with additional experience. Review PMI's full criteria before enrolling to ensure you qualify.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp—an instructor-led course delivered entirely online. Attend interactive sessions over several days or weeks (flexible scheduling available), covering all five process groups and knowledge areas. You'll receive a Certificate of Completion, required for PMI application submission.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Register with PMI and submit your official application, including proof of your 35 contact hours and qualifying project experience. Pay PMI's exam fee at this stage. Double-check all details to avoid delays; PMI reviews applications for completeness before approval.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor support—to build confidence before test day. Schedule your PMP exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. On exam day, you'll answer 180 multiple-choice questions in a computer-based format.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After earning your PMP, commit to the three-year renewal cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, project work, volunteer service, or community engagement. Renew with PMI before expiration to keep your credential active and competitive in your local job market.
